steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and useState from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement for React and useState should be added at the top of the file.
successCriteria: The code must include an import statement that imports both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for building React components with state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but the import statement needs to include both React and useState from 'react'. Make sure you're using the correct syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the AuthFlow component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named AuthFlow that returns null for now.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function called AuthFlow that returns null. This will be the main component for your authentication flow.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the AuthFlow component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthFlow component is defined and returns null.
successCriteria: The code defines a component named AuthFlow (either as a function or arrow function) that returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the AuthFlow component. This will serve as the foundation for your authentication flow.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined a component named AuthFlow that returns null. Check your syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. You need to define a functional component named AuthFlow that returns null.

steps.title: Initialize isLoggedIn state
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthFlow component, use the useState hook to create a state variable called isLoggedIn with an initial value of false.
steps.hint: Remember to use the useState hook you imported earlier. The state variable should be typed as boolean.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthFlow component now has a state variable isLoggedIn that tracks whether the user is logged in, initialized to false.
successCriteria: State variable named isLoggedIn is declared
Uses useState hook with initial value false
State is typed as boolean (explicitly or inferred)
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the isLoggedIn state variable to track authentication status.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've: 1) named the variable 'isLoggedIn', 2) used useState with false as initial value, and 3) typed it as boolean.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Inside the AuthFlow component, use useState to create a boolean state variable called isLoggedIn starting as false.

steps.title: Initialize username state
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthFlow component, create a state variable called 'username' using useState. Initialize it with an empty string and make sure it's typed as string.
steps.hint: You'll need to call useState<string>('') and destructure the returned array into [username, setUsername].
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing a string state
const [username, setUsername] = useState<string>('');
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have two state variables: isLoggedIn (boolean) and username (string).
successCriteria: The code should include a useState call for username with type string and initial value empty string, placed after the isLoggedIn state declaration.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a username state variable that will store the user's name as a string.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using useState<string>('') to properly type the username state as a string with an empty initial value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The username state isn't properly initialized. You need to add a useState call with string type and empty string initial value.

steps.title: Define handleLogin function
steps.instruction: Inside your AuthFlow component, define a function named handleLogin that takes no parameters and returns void. This function should set isLoggedIn to true and set username to a string value (e.g., 'JohnDoe').
steps.hint: Create a function using either function handleLogin() { ... } or const handleLogin = () => { ... } syntax. Inside it, call setIsLoggedIn(true) and setUsername('JohnDoe') (or another string).
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a handleLogin function that updates both isLoggedIn and username states when called.
successCriteria: The code includes a function named handleLogin that calls setIsLoggedIn(true) and setUsername with a string argument.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the handleLogin function that updates both state variables.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but it might be missing one of the required state updates. Make sure it calls both setIsLoggedIn(true) and setUsername('someString').
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleLogin function is not defined correctly. It should be a function that updates both isLoggedIn and username states.

steps.title: Define handleLogout function
steps.instruction: Inside your AuthFlow component, define a function named handleLogout that sets isLoggedIn to false and clears the username to an empty string.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setIsLoggedIn(false) and setUsername('').
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a handleLogout function that properly updates both state variables when called.
successCriteria: The function should be named handleLogout, call setIsLoggedIn(false), and call setUsername('').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Your handleLogout function correctly updates both state variables.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your handleLogout function sets isLoggedIn to false and clears the username.
steps.feedbackWrong: Your handleLogout function doesn't properly update the state. Check that you're calling both state setters correctly.

steps.title: Return a wrapper div
steps.instruction: In the AuthFlow component, return a div element that wraps the existing h1 element.
steps.hint: Make sure the return statement returns a single div element containing the h1.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a div element that wraps the h1 element.
successCriteria: The return statement should output a single div element containing the h1 element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wrapped the h1 in a div, creating a proper JSX structure for your component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're returning a div element that contains the h1 element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't return a div wrapping the h1. Check the return statement structure.

steps.title: Add conditional rendering for auth status
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add conditional rendering that shows different content based on the isLoggedIn state. When isLoggedIn is true, show a welcome message with the username. When false, show a login prompt.
steps.hint: You can use a ternary operator directly in JSX: {isLoggedIn ? (content when true) : (content when false)}
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display different content based on whether the user is logged in or not.
successCriteria: The code should include a ternary operator in the JSX that checks isLoggedIn and renders different content in the true and false branches.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional rendering that shows different content based on the authentication state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the isLoggedIn state in your conditional rendering and showing appropriate content in both branches.
steps.feedbackWrong: The conditional rendering isn't quite right. Remember to use a ternary operator that checks isLoggedIn and shows different content for logged in vs logged out states.

steps.title: Create login form structure
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthFlow component's return statement, add a form element with an input field for username and a submit button. Place this form inside the wrapper div, after the existing h1 element.
steps.hint: Use JSX to create a <form> element containing an <input type="text"> and a <button type="submit">. Remember to keep the existing h1 element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now display a basic login form structure below the 'Auth Flow' heading.
successCriteria: A <form> element is added inside the wrapper div
The form contains an <input type="text"> element
The form contains a <button type="submit"> element
The existing h1 element remains unchanged
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the login form structure with username input and submit button.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've included all required elements: a form with both an input field and a submit button.
steps.feedbackWrong: The login form structure is missing or incomplete. Please add a form element containing an input field and a submit button.

steps.title: Wire login form to handleLogin
steps.instruction: Add an onSubmit handler to the login form that calls the handleLogin function when the form is submitted.
steps.hint: Add onSubmit={handleLogin} to the form element in your JSX.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of wiring a form to a handler
<form onSubmit={handleSubmit}>
  <input type="text" />
  <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
steps.expectedOutcome: The login form will have an onSubmit handler that calls handleLogin when submitted.
successCriteria: The form element includes onSubmit={handleLogin}
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wired the login form to call handleLogin when submitted.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the form's onSubmit attribute is set to call handleLogin.
steps.feedbackWrong: The login form is not properly wired to handleLogin. Add onSubmit={handleLogin} to the form element.

steps.title: Create logged-in welcome message
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add a welcome message that displays the username when the user is logged in. Use the existing isLoggedIn state to conditionally render this message.
steps.hint: You can use a ternary operator or logical && operator to conditionally render JSX based on isLoggedIn. The message should include the username state value.
steps.expectedOutcome: When isLoggedIn is true, a welcome message displaying the username should appear in the UI.
successCriteria: Conditional rendering based on isLoggedIn
Display username state value in message
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a welcome message that displays the username when the user is logged in. This completes the core authentication flow UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the isLoggedIn state to conditionally render the message and displaying the username value from state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The welcome message isn't properly implemented. Remember to use conditional rendering with isLoggedIn and display the username state value in the message.

steps.title: Add logout button and wire to handleLogout
steps.instruction: Add a logout button inside the logged-in welcome message section and wire its onClick event to the handleLogout function.
steps.hint: Place a button element with text like 'Logout' and set its onClick prop to call handleLogout.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding a logout button
<button onClick={handleLogout}>Logout</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A logout button appears when logged in, and clicking it triggers the handleLogout function to reset the auth state.
successCriteria: Add a button element inside the logged-in section
Set the button's onClick prop to handleLogout
Button text should indicate logout action
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the logout button and wired it to the handleLogout function. This completes the basic auth flow with login and logout functionality.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the logout button is inside the logged-in section (after the welcome message) and its onClick prop is correctly set to handleLogout.
steps.feedbackWrong: The logout button is missing or not properly wired. Add a button element with onClick={handleLogout} inside the logged-in section.
